key_claims: Worldwide cases of all-cause dementia are expected to reach approximately 152.8 million by the year 2050.
Potential treatments like anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies will increase the demand on memory clinics and neurologists to quickly identify and stage Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.
Neuropsychological evaluation offers essential information for clinicians and patients.
Current neuropsychological assessments face obstacles such as a lack of trained specialists, long testing batteries, and delays in receiving written reports.
limitations: The source material discusses clinical demand and assessment barriers but does not provide details or data about the specific one-hour test mentioned in the headline.
No specific study design, methodology, or performance metrics for diagnostic tests are included in the provided text.
what_not_to_say: Do not claim that anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies cure Alzheimer's disease.
Do not describe how the one-hour test works, its accuracy, or its specific components, as those details are absent from the text.
Do not state that any specific institution or researcher authored this assessment.
